source.title: CRISP: Persistent Concept Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Tomer Ashuach; Dana Arad; Aaron Mueller; Martin Tutek; Yonatan Belinkov

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes SAE features in LLMs and reports both semantically coherent features and specific examples of features that appear entangled, qualifying claims that SAE features are canonical units.
record.gate_note: The feature analysis in Section 6 and Tables 4–5 bears on V4 and V5. The unlearning benchmark scores and generated outputs evaluate the unlearning method, not superposition geometry or the completeness and stability of SAE features, so they are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: CRISP is an unlearning method built on pretrained SAEs (Llama Scope, Gemma Scope). The paper takes SAE interpretability as given and uses it as a tool. Section 6 inspects only the features CRISP itself selected, reading their Neuronpedia labels and top tokens to show the method is selective. It reports no measure of how well the SAEs recover features, how completely they cover the representation, or how stable features are. It makes no superposition test, and its own results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CRISP beats RMU and ELM on WMDP unlearning while keeping retention and fluency. They add that the features it selects are semantically coherent directions aligned with the target concept. They note, mainly in the appendix, that some SAE features may blend themes or be poorly captured by Neuronpedia explanations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses pretrained SAEs to select and analyze features in LLMs for concept unlearning. It does not reproduce toy-network superposition experiments or measure overlapping directions, interference, or sparsity-dependent geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature analysis is reported for WMDP-Bio at layer 24 for Llama-3.1-8B and layer 14 for Gemma-2-2B. The paper does not report a systematic comparison of feature semantic results across layers or other domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Two of the target features CRISP selected in Gemma-2-2B (4008 and 11127) have Neuronpedia labels (flowers, financial crisis) that do not match all their contexts. On inspection they also activate on viral-replication text and on poisoning or terrorism text. The authors say this reflects either SAE entanglement or limits of the explanations, and do not decide which.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some SAE features in pretrained LLM SAEs activate on semantically distinct themes beyond their automated label (anecdotal, method-selected features).

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The feature-level evidence is qualitative and limited to selected features, one biosecurity domain, and specified layers. The paper notes that feature explanations may be limited and that pretrained SAEs may fail to capture disentangled or interpretable features.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning benchmark scores, generation evaluations, and other method comparisons were omitted because they do not measure the representation claims in these versions.

untested.parts: No toy models and no sparsity-dependent geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
No analysis of other causes of polysemantic neurons.
Pretrained SAEs are used as a tool. Recovery and feature spread are not measured.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not measured.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/tests classification overreads a qualitative sanity check of the method's own feature selection. The features shown were picked by CRISP's contrastive criterion and are interpreted through Neuronpedia's automated labels. No measure of SAE recovery, coverage, completeness or stability appears. The entanglement observation covers two features with an ambiguous attribution. Tables 6–7 give similar qualitative tables for other layers and do not change the assessment.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is tested.
No test of neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of limited capacity, or of importance-dependent allocation of dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

The paper qualitatively examines selected SAE features in two LLMs on the WMDP-Bio domain; it does not measure feature coverage across the models or compare SAE recovery with other dictionaries or representation methods.
The analysis examines semantic coherence and contextual entanglement of selected features, but does not test completeness or stability across prompts, runs, or training stages.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively analyzed selected SAE features and their activation patterns and interpretations.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence of selected target SAE features
rows.value: The authors report that target features capture biosecurity-related concepts, including viral infections, biofilm formation and infection implications, infectious-disease impacts, and mosquito-borne diseases.
rows.note: The authors also list feature-level explanations and top tokens in Table 4. This is qualitative evidence about selected features, not a measurement of overall feature coverage.
rows.check: The features were chosen by CRISP's own contrastive selection (top-k frequency difference, then a ratio threshold). Their coherence rests on Neuronpedia labels. This is a check on the method's selection, not a measure of whether SAEs recover sparse features in LLMs; there is no baseline and no coverage measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively analyzed selected SAE features and their activation patterns and interpretations.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic coherence of selected target SAE features
rows.value: The authors report target features related to viral infections and medical testing, vaccines and immunization, infections, and pandemic impacts.
rows.note: The paper also identifies two features in this analysis as apparently misidentified from their explanations and top tokens, with further contextual activation evidence discussed separately.
rows.check: Same problem as R1. These are method-selected features in Gemma-2-2B, layer 14, described qualitatively by their labels, with no baseline or coverage measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected contextual activations of SAE feature 4008 after its feature explanation and top tokens appeared flower-related.
rows.measure: Qualitative alignment between feature interpretation and contextual activation
rows.value: Although the explanation and top tokens appeared flower-related, the authors report that the feature also activates on texts about viral replication and genome transcription.
rows.note: The authors treat this as possible conceptual entanglement or a limitation of the feature explanation, rather than a simple misclassification.
rows.check: An anecdote about one selected feature (4008). The authors attribute the mismatch either to SAE entanglement or to limits of Neuronpedia's explanations and do not decide between them, so it cannot show that SAE features are or are not canonical units.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected contextual activations of SAE feature 11127 after its feature explanation and top tokens appeared financial-crisis-related.
rows.measure: Qualitative alignment between feature interpretation and contextual activation
rows.value: Although the explanation and top tokens appeared related to financial crises, the authors report activation in contexts involving poisoning, terrorist attacks, and missile alerts.
rows.note: The authors describe this as possible conceptual entanglement or a limitation of the feature explanation.
rows.check: An anecdote about one selected feature (11127), with the same unresolved attribution (SAE entanglement or explanation limits) as R3. It is not a test of completeness or stability.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected target SAE features in Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B on WMDP-Bio
reader_labels.reason: The authors report semantically interpretable target features associated with biosecurity concepts in both models (R1–R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B WMDP-Bio features 4008 and 11127 at layer 14
reader_labels.reason: For these features, contextual activation did not match the apparent feature explanation alone, indicating that selected SAE features can have mixed or context-dependent semantics (R3–R4).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B WMDP-Bio features 4008 and 11127 at layer 14
reader_labels.reason: The reported cross-theme activations show that at least these SAE features are not straightforward, semantically exclusive canonical units (R3–R4).
